voice_notes: Willow is blunt, impatient and irreverent: short exclamations, 'Ugh', 'Ew', 'Heh', calls things dumb or boring, hates reading ('Wow, another book I'll never read!', 'Looks like kindling to me!'), measures everything by whether it burns, and covers fear with bravado ('You don't scare me! Okay, maybe a little.'). She already has a self-copy joke in vanilla, 'Hey! That's my face, %s! Give it back!', which these shadow lines build on. PT-BR keeps her colloquial and spoken ('tô', 'pra', 'Ugh', 'Heh', 'Eca', 'sinistro' for creepy, feminine agreement: 'Eu não tô assustada'). ZH renders her with short, punchy clauses and casual particles (呃 for Ugh, 呵 for Heh, 吓人 for creepy, e.g. 'WX，你这个贪心的破铜烂铁！'). RU makes her a sharp-tongued girl with feminine verb forms and slangy interjections ('Блин, заряда не осталось.', 'Хех', 'Гадость. Дайте два.'), writing е instead of ё as the official file does.

line_notes.codex: Willow burns or mocks every book in the game, so the joke is that this is the first one she'd spare, now that it actually does something.
line_notes.codex_needsfuel: Pays off her Codex line ('worth NOT burning'): once it is empty, it is just kindling to her.
line_notes.no_max_sanity: A fire pun about exhaustion rather than burning things; 'burnt out' works as a double meaning in all four languages.
line_notes.shadow_mine: Vain, bossy and pleased with herself: she compliments her copy and orders it around in one breath.
line_notes.shadow_other: Picks up her 'that's my face' rivalry and her 'creepier than the real one' attitude, then insults the stranger's copy by comparing it with her own.
